calibration_rulings.title: The title of a park named after a PLACE ('Al-Ahsa National Park', 'Jawatha Park', 'Al-Koot Park' …): no approved title is of this kind.
calibration_rulings.binds: The six titles of the batch and every mention of the six names in bodies and questions; kanzan-park::body (the official name, in marks). Every later park named after a place.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A park named after a place takes ruling N43's pattern, as the beach titles of ruling N84 do: the place name as its termbase key, the Urdu possessive, the generic of ruling N69 — the six titles of the batch as they stand: «الاحساء کی قومی تفریح گاہ», «جواثا کی تفریح گاہ», «عین النجم کی تفریح گاہ», «الشیبانی / المشقر کی تفریح گاہ», «جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ (الشعبہ)», «الکوت کی تفریح گاہ» (kanzan-park's, mushaqar's and najm-park's titles as items N103, N112 and N117 word them); the official name in kanzan-park's body is built the same way, «جبل الشعبہ کی تفریح گاہ»; an adjective of the name stands before the generic. The title inflects like any phrase. It is feminine by its generic. Ruling N85 (no possessive after a PERSON's name) is untouched. B and C are refused: B is attested once with this generic, C is the order of a generic that opens a name. THE COST, stated and charged on national-park: with the ruled noun the title does not say 'national park' to the reader. That is ruling N69's cost and the owner's rule on loans, not this pattern's, and a batch judge reopens neither. FOR THE OWNER, as a decision (notes): whether a park, and a national park in particular, takes the loan on /ur/ — the entry of the generic itself says the loan 'would have to pass the loan test' on a park page, and its three conditions are argued in the notes. All six title entries stay pending: no Urdu page names any of these parks. ROUND 2: The six titles are listed as they stand, and the guard names the three that other items word (proof pass on round 1, finding 2). The question for the owner — whether a national park takes the loan — is no longer only in the notes: it is item N119 (owner_decision). The pattern is not reopened.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title of a park named after a place begins with the place name as its termbase key writes it, then the possessive, then the generic; verbs and adjectives that agree with it are feminine; no possessive after a person's name (ruling N85). Three titles are worded by other items and hold as those items word them: kanzan-park's closes with a second name in a bracket (item N103); mushaqar's has two names and a slash until the owner answers (item N112); najm-park's spells the spring as the Arabic title does until the owner answers (item N117).

calibration_rulings.title: The generic of two titles whose English says 'Park' and whose Arabic says garden (najm-park, koot-park); and, through ruling N65, the gender of koot-park's Hours value.
calibration_rulings.binds: najm-park::title; koot-park::title; koot-park::practical[0].value; every agreeing form on the two pages. Every later page whose English title says 'Park' for an Arabic garden.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A on both pages. The Urdu title mirrors title_en (the style rule for titles; the precedent of jabri-mosque, where the English generic was followed against the Arabic's): «عین النجم کی تفریح گاہ», «الکوت کی تفریح گاہ», feminine. koot-park's Hours value is therefore the feminine string of ruling N65, «24 گھنٹے کھلی رہتی ہے», byte for byte — the first use of that string on the site; it enters the translation memory with this page, with the note 'feminine title' (rulings N65 and N87). The text of koot-park says the garden noun where its sources say garden, masculine. That a title and its text differ in the noun is the ENGLISH source's own, logged as a source defect and not evened out. FOR THE OWNER, one line (candidate C for koot-park alone): the garden noun in the title — then the key, the gender and the Hours value change together to the masculine pair — if he wants title and text to agree; it is what the Arabic calls the place. ROUND 2: A stands for najm-park, on which neither reader remarked. koot-park's title — the garden noun or the park noun — is put to the owner as its own item, N121 (owner_decision), with both readers' evidence; until he answers the text is as ruled here, and the Hours value the feminine string of ruling N65.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: on koot-park every form that agrees with the title is feminine and every form that agrees with the garden noun masculine; the Hours value is the second string of ruling N65 byte for byte.

calibration_rulings.title: kanzan-park's title: both source titles carry a SECOND NAME in a bracket ('Kanzan Adventure Park (Al-Shu'bah)'); the stage checker reports a bracket in a title as a gloss in a heading.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::title; the termbase key of the page (it carries the bracket).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A — THE TITLE KEEPS THE BRACKET BOTH SOURCE TITLES CARRY: «جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ (الشعبہ)». This is a new case, not a reopening: a bracket that holds a second NAME which BOTH source titles carry in a bracket is not a gloss; it stands at the end of the title, holds the name as its termbase key and nothing else, and is the only kind of bracket a title may carry. The gloss rules stand untouched for what they were made for: no gloss, no Urdu generic and no bracket of any other kind in a title, a kicker, a label or a question, and no bracket directly after a jabal name (here the bracket follows the generic of the park). The title follows the Arabic name ('Mountain'; the English-only 'Adventure' is not written), on the approved key of the mountain. THE CHECKER'S FINDING IS CARRIED, not answered by reshaping the title: I hold that the probe reaches further than the rule it guards and I report it; I did not edit the tool. FALLBACK, named so that a later round does not have to find it: if the coordinator holds the two guards to their letter, or the probe is not taught the case, the title is D, «جبل کنزان / الشعبہ کی تفریح گاہ» — both names kept, the device of the page's own summary — with the cost the first reader showed on mushaqar's slash (the possessive attaches to the second name only); never B, which drops a name both sources carry. ROUND 2: A CONFIRMED, on its merits and on the second reader's evidence, and no longer carried as a finding. THE EXCEPTION IS WRITTEN WHERE THE GUARDS ARE: the two guards that bar a bracket in a title by their letter are carried in this file as entries P3a and P3c-labels, each with this item's exception in its guard, so that each ruling, its guard and its notes agree and stand alone. THE FALLBACK IS CORRECTED, on the proof pass's finding 11: D is WITHDRAWN (its possessive falls on the second name alone, here a village's key). If a title without a bracket is ever forced, it is the order of the page's own summary, «الشعبہ / جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ», which puts the possessive on the mountain and departs from the order of both source titles; B, which drops a name both sources carry, stays the last resort. The key in termbase_final is byte for byte the title. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14), proof pass on round 2, note 6: two rulings still restate the old letter "no bracket in a title" and are read under this exception: ruling A of N70 (a jabal name takes no bracket, in title or body; it binds pages whose source glosses the name, and defers to the guards of P3a and P3c as amended here), and b0-ui's own P3c-labels (round 3), which governs the interface strings, not the attraction batches. Neither binds kanzan-park's title; neither is reworded.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a title carries a bracket only where both source titles close with a second name in a bracket; the bracket holds that name and nothing else and closes the title, and the whole title is a termbase key, byte for byte. No bracket follows a jabal name directly. The stage checker's heading probe tests the same conditions since round 2 of b7.

calibration_rulings.title: A number of a lakh or more that BOTH sources write in words ('two million trees', the Arabic dual): digits with the scale word, or words?
calibration_rulings.binds: national-park::body (change 2). Every later number of a lakh or more that both sources spell.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B: «بیس لاکھ درختوں» (change 2). A number that both sources write in WORDS is written in words in the Urdu, in the Urdu scale and without a scale loan — as the same paragraph keeps the sources' 'twenty kilometres' in words and the batch their 'eight gardens', 'three bridges' and 'two lakes'. Rulings P10 and N66 are not reopened: each is worded for a FIGURE of the source (the guard of P10: 'where the English or Arabic carries a figure followed by million'; ruling N66: a figure 'the English gives in bare digits') and gives that figure digits with the scale word. Where the sources give a figure, the digits stay («4,500», «1,100», «1,500»; the home page's large figure). The value is unchanged. This is decided on the form of the sources and on the site's rule for figures, and it is also what both checks accept: said plainly, so that nobody has to wonder whether the text was bent — it was not, since A would have put a figure into the Urdu where neither source has one.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a number the sources write in words is written in words, with the Urdu scale word after it and no scale loan; a figure of the source keeps digits (rulings P10 and N66). The stage checker and build check C62 compare figures only and pass a number in words.

calibration_rulings.title: A part of a single year ('in late 2022', 'in late 2020', 'in mid-2015').
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::body, koot-park::body, najm-park::body. Every later part of a year.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The closings that rulings N11 and N20 give a century and a decade serve a single year: «2022 کے اواخر میں», «2020 کے اواخر میں», «2015 کے وسط میں» — a bare year (ruling N12), no word for 'year' before it. One family of closings for a century, a decade and a year, and the Arabic's own word for 'late'. B stays on record for whoever reopens ruling N11, for all three scales at once.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a part of a year is the bare year with one of the three closings of ruling N11.

calibration_rulings.title: The loan test of ruling P16-test for the two rides of kanzan-park that stages 1 to 5 described in native words — the zipline and the cable car — and for the loan «اسٹیشن» that already stands in the text.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::body (round 1's change 8; round 2's change 3 for the order of the cable car's attributes; the zipline unchanged from stage 1 until the owner decides item N116-zipline-loan-or-description). Every later page that names a cable car.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE TEST, condition by condition, one account. (1) CABLE CAR: THE LOAN STANDS — «کیبل کار», feminine (the press writes it so), plural «کیبل کاریں»; in the text «… تین اسٹیشنوں اور 1,500 میٹر لمبے راستے والی کیبل کار بھی شامل ہے» (round 1's change 8, re-ordered by round 2's change 3). All three conditions are met, the third by a dictionary entry: the dictionary's page for the English term gives the loan first, and its first word is an Urdu headword. Its entry cites P16 with this evidence and is PENDING (round 2, on the proof pass's finding 3), as the line's practice for an admitted loan without an Urdu headword page (ruling P16-test: the browser loan; ruling N90). SAID FOR THE OWNER, whose rule (P16) asks for an entry that cites a dictionary entry: the entry cited is the dictionary's English-to-Urdu page and the headword of the first word; no Urdu headword page of the compound was obtained. If he will have no loan here, the dictionary's own native word is «تار گاڑی», which no reference page uses. The chain's description is WITHDRAWN (a retired key of this entry); it is not written again. (2) ZIPLINE: THE NATIVE DESCRIPTION STAYS IN THE TEXT — «رسی سے لٹک کر ہوا میں پھسلنے کی سواری» — and what the ride is called is NOT ruled here: it is the owner's decision, item N116-zipline-loan-or-description. Ruling N90 admitted a loan without a dictionary headword once, where a reader had been MISLED on a fact the owner guards; here the reader decoded the description rightly and nothing guarded hangs on it, which is the case of ruling N100 (the caravan). No second description is coined. (3) STATION: «اسٹیشن» stays (plural unchanged; oblique plural «اسٹیشنوں»). It is the settled word, the dictionary writes it in its own definitions, and Urdu has no common word for the stop of a cable car; its entry stays PENDING for want of a headword page and is flagged for the owner with the two rides. ROUND 2: The loan stands and the sentence is re-ordered as the proof pass proposed; the two loans of the sentence are pending alike. Nothing else in this item moves. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled" and lists it for the owner; it is entered with its open question stated, as b6 entered N93, N94 and N99). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 12): N106: the cable car and the station are admitted loans with pending entries (no Urdu headword page).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, checklist item 9: the admitted loans of the page are the termbase entries for the cable car and its station; both entries are pending — the first cites P16 with an English-to-Urdu dictionary page, the press and the reference; the second wants a headword page. The cable car's attributes stand in the order «تین اسٹیشنوں اور 1,500 میٹر لمبے راستے والی کیبل کار». The withdrawn description of the cable car is a retired key of this entry (read by the stage checker). What may not be written for the zipline is in the guard of item N116-zipline-loan-or-description.

calibration_rulings.title: The set term the Arabic uses and the English paraphrases ('the accounts of Arabia's celebrated battle-days'): how it stands in the sentence.
calibration_rulings.binds: mushaqar::body. Every later set term of this kind.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The Urdu meaning first, the term after it as what those battles are called, in quotation marks: «اس کا ذکر عربوں کی ان مشہور لڑائیوں کے تذکروں میں آتا ہے جو “ایام العرب” کہلاتی ہیں۔» It is how the Urdu reference introduces the term; the marks are those of a term cited as what something is called (ruling N16, point 5); the meaning is given by the sentence itself, so no bracket is owed and the entry's gloss field stays null (ruling P3b is for a NAME with no currency in Urdu). D stays on record as the wording without the term. WHY THE PAGE'S MARKS ARE AS THEY ARE, for the reader's item 45: a name both sources quote stands in marks (item N113), a term cited as a term stands in marks (this item), a name in use stands bare.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker (read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs): the key «ایام العرب» in the direct case stands between U+201C and U+201D. For the proofreader, not machine-read: its meaning stands before it in the same sentence and no bracket follows it.

calibration_rulings.title: kanzan-park body: 'the massif of Al-Shu'bah Mountain (historically Kanzan)' — how the historical name is said, and whether the sentence stands on its merits or to quiet a probe.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, unchanged: «… جبل الشعبہ کا پہاڑی سلسلہ ہے۔ اس پہاڑ کا تاریخی نام کنزان ہے۔» The sentence says what both sources say and no more, in the approved page's own words for the massif and the mountain; Urdu needs a noun there, so the generic stands on its merits. That a massif is then called a mountain is the sources' (logged). For the tools, not for the text, as stage 4 reported: the probe of ruling P3a reads the first word of a title and so holds a park named after a mountain to the rule for mountains.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the massif and the mountain are said with the nouns of the approved kanzan page; no bracket follows the jabal name.

calibration_rulings.title: The last clause of kanzan-park's English body, which has no Arabic: 'and full operation is yet to be confirmed'.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::body (round 1's change 9; round 2's change 4).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, with the sources' 'still' said by another word: «تعمیر کے بقیہ مراحل بدستور جاری ہیں، اور اس کے مکمل طور پر کھلنے کی تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے۔» (round 1's change 9 took the doubled adverb out of the first clause; round 2's change 4 puts back the sources' 'still' with «بدستور», the proof pass's word, so that «ابھی» stands once, where the predicate of ruling N99 has it). The clause is rendered text and the English is the translation source, so it is translated; it borrows only the predicate of ruling N99-pending-confirmation-sentence, so that the site says 'not yet confirmed' in one way, and it promises nothing — no date, no future tense. It is NOT ruling N99's fixed sentence and NOT the short form of open item P4. C (leaving it out, as the Arabic and the Chinese line do) and D are refused. Its register and its two readings are the source's and follow whatever the owner decides for ruling N99 (ruling P25). Logged with the page's first defect.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the clause ends in the predicate of ruling N99 letter for letter; it carries no date and no future tense; «ابھی» stands once in the sentence, in the predicate, and the first clause carries the sources' 'still' as «بدستور».

calibration_rulings.title: Two bodies on national-park: a ministry of ONE field ('a Ministry of Agriculture project'), which ruling N98 left to this page; and a national centre whose name is a list of two tasks.
calibration_rulings.binds: national-park::body (round 1's change 0 for the sentence of the centre; the ministry unchanged, and from round 2 the owner's decision, item N120). Every later ministry of one field, once the owner has answered N120.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A FOR BOTH BODIES, AND THE SENTENCE OF THE CENTRE RE-ORDERED. (1) THE MINISTRY: «زراعت کی وزارت», feminine — the build of rulings N44, N68 and N98 (the field, the Urdu possessive, the noun last), which ruling N98 itself calls 'the ordinary Urdu for a ministry of agriculture'; the site's two ministries are then built alike, and 'Saudi' is not added. The reader's order is the reference's and is the OWNER'S one-line option: «وزارت زراعت کے ایک منصوبے سے». The entry stays pending for that reason. (2) THE CENTRE: the description stands as stage 4 has it, «سبزے کے فروغ اور صحرا کے پھیلاؤ کی روک تھام کا قومی مرکز», masculine, no quotation marks (ruling N16: a named body stands outside marks), the list closed before the noun (ruling N98). What the reader lost was not the name but its place: the sentence now opens with what is overseen and the description follows as its agent (change 0). Its length — twelve words — and the narrowing of 'vegetation cover' to greenery are the cost of plain words for a body nobody names in Urdu, charged on the page; C stays on record. ROUND 2: (1) THE MINISTRY: the wording stays as above until the owner answers; which order a ministry of one field takes is now his decision, item N120 (owner_decision), with both readers' evidence. (2) THE CENTRE: round 1's order stays — it is the sources' order with their relative — and is charged on the page. Inside the rulings nothing marks where a twelve-word description begins (ruling N16 keeps a named body out of marks), and a third order would be one more unread guess at the same cost. FOR THE OWNER, one line: the body's name in marks, or a short Urdu name for it, would let a reader see where it begins. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled" and lists it for the owner; it is entered with its open question stated, as b6 entered N93, N94 and N99). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 11): N110: the centre's name in marks, or a short Urdu name — two readers lost the thread in two orders.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a ministry is named with its field or fields first, the possessive and the noun last; the centre's description is byte for byte its termbase key, carries no marks, and follows the words for its oversight.

calibration_rulings.title: The 'humanising cities' programme, a NAME that both sources quote and neither explains (koot-park summary and body).
calibration_rulings.binds: koot-park::summary (change 11), koot-park::body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the planning term in the plain words of ruling N79, applied to cities, inside the marks ruling N16 gives the short name of a programme, with the Arabic's noun after the closing mark: «“شہروں کو لوگوں کے لیے بہتر بنانے” کے منصوبے». It is always in the oblique in the text. IN THE SUMMARY the frame is now the English's 'part of' the programme, «… کے منصوبے کا حصہ ہے» (change 11), one link shorter than the Arabic's 'one of the gardens of'; the body keeps the count of eight. B (a literal adjective as a name) was refused of a road by ruling N79 and is on record for the owner: «“انسان دوست شہر” منصوبہ». That the name sounds strange is the cost of a planning term neither source explains (ruling N79 says the same of the road), charged on the page. ROUND 2: A stands; the chain is cured (round 1's change 11, unremarked by the second reader). That the name does not sound like a name is now said by two readers of two: charged, and the literal name B stays the owner's option.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the programme's name stands inside its marks at both mentions, with the noun for the project outside them; nothing about the programme's works is added.

calibration_rulings.title: mushaqar's title: the English has the former name, a slash, the present name and a generic ('Al-Shaibani / Al-Mushaqar Park'); the Arabic title is the present name alone.
calibration_rulings.binds: mushaqar::title — unchanged from stage 1 until the owner decides.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE WORDING, ruled for the text until the owner answers: A, «الشیبانی / المشقر کی تفریح گاہ» — the Urdu title mirrors the structure of title_en, as the style rule for titles asks and as the German and Russian lines did; both names are built from the Arabic with their articles. THE TITLE ITSELF IS THE OWNER'S DECISION, because what misleads the reader is the English title, which differs from the Arabic title and from the order of its own body: does the page carry the present name alone? If yes: B, «المشقر کی تفریح گاہ» — the name the page's own text uses, the Arabic title's one name with the generic, the Chinese line's title — with the key, the alternative text of the gallery image and a proof pass and blind read of the title; the English title should then change too. THE JUDGE'S RECOMMENDATION: B. C (the present name first, with the slash) keeps the slash's cost. ROUND 2: Unchanged in the text: A until the owner answers. THE RECOMMENDATION, B (the present name alone, «المشقر کی تفریح گاہ»), is firmer: two readers of two are unsure which name is the place's, and the slash also breaks the breadcrumb's steps. If he takes B, the English title should change too. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN. The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 4): N112: mushaqar's title the present name alone, «المشقر کی تفریح گاہ»? Two readers of two; the slash also breaks the breadcrumb. Recommended yes.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: in the body the present name stands alone with the generic and the former name in a clause of its own; the title's key stands byte for byte in the title only.

calibration_rulings.title: Two quoted names on mushaqar, built two ways: the fort's second name, whose generic translates, and the modern building's name, which keeps its Arabic generic; and the summary's common noun for that building.
calibration_rulings.binds: mushaqar::summary, mushaqar::body.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Each name stands in the quotation marks BOTH sources give it, at every mention: «“قلعہ ہجر”» with the one Urdu word the page has for the fort (the English translates this generic, and the termbase has one word for fort, fortress and stronghold), and «“قصر المشقر”» with the Arabic generic that ruling N14 keeps in the name of a palace. A second name that both sources quote stands in marks whether or not its generic translates; ruling N72's sentence that 'a second name that carries an Urdu generic stays bare' speaks of names the sources do not quote, and is not touched. The summary's common noun is «محل» ('a palace'; the Arabic has the bare common noun): the word's second place in the text after qasr-ibrahim, forced by the source's own common noun and recorded in its entry; it never stands next to a name that keeps the Arabic generic. calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker (read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs): the key «قصر المشقر» in the direct case stands between U+201C and U+201D; the key «قلعہ ہجر» in the direct case stands between U+201C and U+201D. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the Urdu word for a palace does not stand next to either name.

calibration_rulings.title: mushaqar's area line: 'east of Al-Ahsa' — a part of Al-Ahsa, or a direction from it?

calibration_rulings.ruling: A, on the page's own text, as ruling N74 decided for thulaim: «القارہ گاؤں کے قریب، الاحساء کے مشرقی حصے میں». The line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition (ruling N30; the checker's note of ruling P20 on it is expected). It still chooses one of the Arabic's two readings where the English says a direction: counted under accuracy, and the English wording is logged. B is the fallback if the owner says the park lies east of Al-Ahsa and not in it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the line says a part of Al-Ahsa and ends in a postposition.

calibration_rulings.title: اسم الجنس داخل علم مركّب («جبل»): الاسم يُنقحر كاملاً، والگلوس بالحاجة — لا قوس حيث اسم الجنس نفسه كلمة أوردية
calibration_rulings.binds: كل صفحة يحمل عنوانها «جبل»، والمبدأ (الگلوس بالحاجة) لكل علم مركّب ‖ b7, ROUND 2: kanzan-park::title, under the exception of item N103.
calibration_rulings.ruling: (1) يُنقحر الاسم كاملاً في العنوان وفي المتن؛ اسم الجنس داخله لا يُترجم جزءاً من الاسم ولا يُكرَّر («جبل القارہ پہاڑ» ممنوع). (2) الگلوس يُستحقّ بالحاجة: اسم الجنس الذي هو كلمة معجمية أوردية بالمعنى نفسه لا يأخذ قوساً، و«جبل» منها (مدخل ریختہ يعرّفها اسماً مذكراً معناه «پہاڑ، کوہ»). وبدل القوس يرد اسم الجنس الأوردي «پہاڑ» منفرداً مرة على الأقل في المتن، بعيداً عن الاسم. (3) تُعدَّل `gloss_regel` إلى: مرة لكل مصطلح اسمُ جنسه ليس كلمة أوردية بذلك المعنى. أما صيغة گلوس اسم الجنس المعتم فبند مفتوح (P3c). السند: القارئ الأول لقي «جبل القارہ (القارہ پہاڑ)» فقال إن القوس يشرح الكلمة الوحيدة التي يعرفها وإنه بدا له لحظةً اسماً ثانياً؛ والقارئان الثاني والثالث قرآ الصفحة بلا قوس ولم يسأل أحدهما ما «جبل». ‖ AMENDED IN b7, ROUND 2 (item N103), in its guard only: the last clause, 'the title never carries a bracket', now names its one exception, a second name both source titles carry in a closing bracket (kanzan-park: «جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ (الشعبہ)», where the bracket follows the park's generic, not the jabal name). The ruling's subject — a gloss of a generic that is itself an Urdu word — and everything else in it is unchanged. The stage checker's heading probe was taught the same exception by the coordinator.
calibration_rulings.guard: البند 10 من المرحلة 5 وفاحص المراحل: لا «(» مباشرةً بعد اسمٍ يبدأ بـ«جبل »؛ وفي صفحة كهذه ترد الكلمة «پہاڑ» مرة على الأقل في المتن ولا تلاصق الاسم؛ والعنوان لا يحمل قوساً إلا في حالة واحدة (البند N103 من الدفعة b7): اسمٌ ثانٍ يُغلِق به العنوانان المصدريان الإنجليزي والعربي كلاهما بين قوسين، فيُغلَق العنوان الأوردي بزوج قوسين واحد لا يحوي إلا ذلك الاسم، والعنوان كله مفتاح في المعجم حرفاً بحرف؛ ولا گلوس ولا اسم جنس أوردي بين قوسين في عنوان أبداً، ولا قوس مباشرةً بعد اسم يبدأ بـ«جبل ». — In English: the title carries no bracket, save the one case of item N103 of b7: a second name with which BOTH source titles close in a bracket; the Urdu title then closes with one bracket pair that holds that name and nothing else, and the whole title is a termbase key byte for byte. No gloss and no Urdu generic stands in a bracket in a title, ever, and no bracket follows a jabal name directly.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: الحاكم; guard amended by the b7 judge, round 2, 2026-10-14
